title: NodeGSM plugin
description: plugins/<game>/plugin.json - describes how NodeGSM installs, runs, configures and monitors one game server.

id.description: Unique id. Must equal the folder name.

name.description: Title shown in the game browser, e.g. Palworld Dedicated Server.

description.description: One or two sentences for the game browser / website card.

author.description: The maker of the plugin, shown on the catalogue card.

contributors.description: Other people who improved the plugin.

summary.description: One line for the catalogue card (defaults to the start of description).

url.description: Homepage, docs or repository of the plugin/game.

docs.description: Documentation links: official and unofficial guides for creating/running this server. Shown in the in-app game browser and on the website.

title.description: Link text, e.g. Dedicated server guide.

type.description: official = published by the game/server developer; unofficial = community wiki, guide, forum, video ...

description.description: Optional one-liner about what the page covers.

media.description: Files inside the plugin folder shown in the game browser and on the website.

platforms.description: Operating systems this game is known to run on (default: Windows only). NodeGSM refuses to create a server for a platform that is not listed. 'linux' needs the Linux build of the server; add run.linux / install.linux where it differs.

install.description: How to get the server files. Shorthands: {type: steamcmd, appId} or {type: manual}; or a list of steps. Optional "linux": same shape, used instead on Linux.

exe.description: Server executable relative to the server files folder (use /).

command.description: Run this program instead (e.g. java); exe is then only used to check the install.

workingDir.description: Working directory relative to the server files folder.

stdin.description: false for srcds/hlds (console input breaks them).

stopCommand.description: Text written to the console to stop gracefully.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the server process; {serverFiles} is replaced by the server files folder.

linux.description: Overrides used on Linux (exe, command, workingDir, args, stdin, stopCommand, env). Keys that are not set fall back to the plain run values; setting exe without command drops the plain command.

gslt.description: Show a Game Server Login Token field.

configs.description: Config files users can edit in the app (INI, JSON, ...). Any number.

path.description: Relative to the server files folder.

template.description: File in the plugin folder copied when the user clicks Create.

protect.description: Keys/lines kept when this file is synced to cluster members, e.g. port, rcon.*

metrics.description: Extra live numbers (FPS, tick rate, entities ...) shown as selectable columns on the Dashboard. Each is read with a regex from the console or a declared log, optionally by sending a console command on a timer.

source.description: console, log:<id of a declared log>, or rcon:<command> (command sent through RCON every intervalSec; the reply is parsed with pattern).

pattern.description: JavaScript regex with ONE capture group holding the number, e.g. fps[:= ]+([0-9.]+). The newest match wins.

command.description: Console command sent every intervalSec so the game prints the value (needs run.stdin).

staleSec.description: Show - when no new value arrived for this long.

kind.description: tick = the server's tick rate / tick time (TPS, tick rate, FPS, ms per tick). Shown as the Tick column, header stat, dashboard tile and chart, coloured by thresholds.

tickTarget.description: Healthy value, e.g. 20 (TPS), 64 (tick rate), 50 (ms per tick). Used for colours when no thresholds are given.

higherIsBetter.description: false for times (ms per tick): bigger is worse.

badBelow.description: higherIsBetter: red below this value (<= warnBelow).

warnAbove.description: higherIsBetter false: yellow above this value.

badAbove.description: higherIsBetter false: red above this value (>= warnAbove).

patternFlags.description: RegExp flags, default "i" (g / y are ignored).

rconConsole.description: source rcon:<command>: id of the rcon console to use (default: the first one).

rconSource.description: source rcon:<command>: inline rcon:<port>:<password> (placeholders allowed) instead of a console.

cluster.description: Optional. Cluster behaviour: what must stay unique per member server and what to clean.

protectedConfigKeys.description: Config keys never overwritten when a config is synced to cluster members, e.g. port, rcon.*

clearFolders.description: Folders cleaned by the cluster 'clear folders' action.

preserve.description: Paths (relative to the server files folder) never overwritten by a cluster update, e.g. saves.

backup.description: Optional. Neat-pick backup presets and exclusions.

exclude.description: Paths / wildcard patterns left out of backups.

events.description: Optional. Extra game-specific events that can be logged / sent to Discord.

logging.description: Optional. What the NGSM event log should read from the game.

logFiles.description: Log files (relative paths, wildcards allowed) the game writes. Declared only - scanning log files is not implemented yet.

regex.description: JavaScript regex matched against each line.

consoles.description: Optional. Extra consoles shown in the Console tab.

id.description: Unique in consoles[]; main is reserved for the game console.

source.description: type log: id of a declared log. type rcon: rcon:<port>:<password>, each part a literal or a {placeholder} ({port}, {configId:key}, {key}); see PLUGINS.md.

validateArgs.description: Per-installer arguments used for Validate, e.g. { "steamcmd": "validate" }.

autoClear.description: Rules that delete old files periodically.

logs.description: Log files shown live in the app. Any number. Wildcards * ? allowed in the file name (newest match is followed).

relPath.description: Relative path, no .. and not absolute.

recursive.description: Also clean sub-folders (cluster clear folders). Default false.

arg.description: A string, or an array of strings that is kept or dropped as a group when a {placeholder} is empty.

platform.description: steamcmd: force the Steam depot platform (+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType); only sent when it differs from the host.
